title: Terrestrial Energy Reports Q3 2026 Net Loss of $11.0 Million
summary: Terrestrial Energy reported a Q3 2026 net loss of $11.0 million, versus $9.4 million in Q2, and held $276.3 million in cash and short-term investments.
body_markdown:
Cash burn was $7.1 million, an increase of $0.7 million compared with the second quarter, which the company said largely reflects higher R&D activity associated with fuel development and testing. Total liabilities were $8.6 million. The company had 105.9 million shares issued and outstanding, unchanged from the second quarter end, and after quarter end it authorized a share repurchase program of up to $25 million of its common stock, funded with existing cash on hand.


The release also said Terrestrial Energy was selected as the advanced nuclear technology supplier for Ameresco, Inc.'s power project at the U.S. Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland. It submitted its Graphite Topical Report to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission and, after quarter end, its Thermal and Electric Facility Topical Report.


## Why It Matters for IMSR


According to the company, the second submission completes its 2026 guidance of at least three Topical Reports, and the Ameresco selection is the second IMSR Plant project it has disclosed this year, in line with its guidance to announce details on one to three additional projects. "Our selection for Ameresco's project with the U.S. Army extends our commercial pipeline into the federal government and defense," said Chief Executive Officer Simon Irish.
